title: SYSK Distraction Playlist: How Terraforming Will Work
summary: A "distraction playlist" rerun-style episode of Stuff You Should Know on terraforming. The hosts open with banter about Click and Clack (Tom and Ray Magliozzi) and overpopulation, then discuss exoplanets and the Goldilocks zone, and why terraforming is distinct from building lunar or orbital bases. They cover Mars (its day length, lost atmosphere from a dead core and magnetic field, the CO2 polar ice caps, Michio Kaku's mirror idea, cyanobacteria to make oxygen, nitrogen delivery via comets, Martin Fogg's book), Venus (sunshade, freezing the atmosphere to slow rotation, floating cities, extremophile thermophiles), the Moon, and a Kardashev-style civilization scale. The episode closes with a Thanksgiving-season segment thanking listeners for gifts.

segments.title: Opening banter and overpopulation
segments.summary: Hosts open with greetings, remember Click and Clack (Tom and Ray Magliozzi), and discuss a study on global population growth and the overpopulation debate that leads to looking to other planets.

segments.title: Exoplanets and the Goldilocks zone
segments.summary: Discussion of the Interstellar movie, NASA's Kepler Observatory exoplanet search, the habitable Goldilocks zone, and why reaching nearby exoplanets is impractical given light-year distances.

segments.title: What terraforming is
segments.summary: Terraforming is defined as turning a planet, moon, or asteroid into a habitable environment, distinct from building bases or floating cities. The hosts mention earlier short videos on terraforming and lunar bases, and Russia's lunar base plans.

segments.title: Time scales and Michio Kaku's CO2 idea
segments.summary: The hosts discuss how long terraforming could take and Michio Kaku's proposal to melt CO2 under Mars's surface to start a greenhouse effect, along with the risk of a runaway greenhouse effect.

segments.title: Why Mars was habitable and lost its atmosphere
segments.summary: Mars's day length is close to Earth's, and it once had water, volcanism, and asteroid-delivered gases. Volcanic recycling stopped and a cooled core lost the magnetic field, letting solar wind strip the atmosphere.

segments.title: Mars steps: CO2 ice caps, mirrors, and cyanobacteria
segments.summary: Melting the polar dry ice with mirrors to thicken the atmosphere and warm the planet, then introducing water and cyanobacteria to convert CO2 into oxygen. Estimates of a couple hundred years for surface water and about forty thousand years for breathable oxygen are discussed.

segments.title: Mars pressure, nitrogen, and Martin Fogg
segments.summary: Discussion of Mars's thin air pressure, the need for nitrogen, the idea of delivering ammonia-based ice comets and exploding them, and Martin Fogg's book on planetary environments favoring gradual, directed atmosphere building over a runaway greenhouse.

segments.title: Venus: sunshade, rotation, and floating cities
segments.summary: Venus is hot and has a very long day. Ideas include a giant sunshade, freezing the atmosphere and blowing it off to speed rotation, lack of water, extremophile thermophiles, and a floating pressurized geodesic city above the clouds. The Kardashev scale is referenced for energy needs.

segments.title: Moon and shell-around-planet ideas
segments.summary: The Moon is considered for its proximity and small size but judged less viable. The hosts discuss the idea of enclosing a planet in a shell and conclude Mars is the likeliest candidate, with the comet sling project in Texas mentioned.

segments.title: Search pointer
segments.summary: Hosts point listeners to the website to search for more on terraforming.

segments.title: Thanksgiving listener gifts
segments.summary: Hosts thank listeners who sent gifts including Australian candy, puzzles, mugs, bookends, chopsticks for salamanders, and a Clyde Avery Thomas birth announcement, and wish a happy Thanksgiving.
